reconstructed_theorem_text: For every complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space E, the squared-norm function x ↦ ‖x‖² is integrable with respect to stdGaussian E, and its integral is Module.finrank ℝ E.
objects: A complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space E; the standard Gaussian probability measure stdGaussian E; the squared-norm function x ↦ ‖x‖².
domains: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure and is complete; x ranges over E; integrability and integration are with respect to stdGaussian E.
quantifiers: Universally quantified over every complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space E.
assumptions: E is complete and finite-dimensional over ℝ, carries a real inner product and Borel structure, and stdGaussian E is the centered Gaussian probability measure with identity covariance.
conclusion: The function x ↦ ‖x‖² is Bochner integrable under stdGaussian E, and ∫ x, ‖x‖² ∂(stdGaussian E) = Module.finrank ℝ E.
scopes: Both the integrability assertion and the integral are over all x ∈ E with respect to stdGaussian E; Module.finrank is taken over ℝ.
constant_dependencies: The value of the integral depends on E only through its real vector-space dimension Module.finrank ℝ E; there are no further parameters.
